To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the small proteoglycan biglycan and the small leucine rich proteoglycan decorin are expressed in rabbit ligaments and that their expression is age-dependent.

the distribution of small leucine rich proteoglycants (SLRPs) biglycan (big) and decorin (dec) in rabbit knee collateral and cruciate (Cr) ligaments and meniscus (M) changes with age and that the distribution of the mRNAs (mRNAs) of these PGs changes with age in a similar manner to the PGs themselves.

the small leucine‐rich proteoglycants (SLRPGs) bigylycan and decorins are found in the extracellular matrix (ECM) of rabbit knee joint ligaments and meniscal tissues, but the localization and relative amounts of these SLRPGs are different in different tissues and at different ages.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role that the extracellular matrix (ECM) plays in determining tissue function.
the role of proteoglycane (PGs) in the development, maintenance, and repair of ligaments and meniscus of the knee joint.
the role of the proteoglyc can (PG), biglycan, in the development and aging of ligaments and meniscus of the knee joint.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
biglycan and/or decorin are not required for the development and/or maintenance of the structure and function of the knee joint ligaments and meniscus.
in the ligamentous and meniscal tissues of the rabbit knee, biglycan is expressed in a more uniform fashion than is decorin.
biglycan is a major component in the extracellular matrix of the collagen bundles in the ligaments and meniscus.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the small leucine rich proteoglycants (SLRPGs) are present in the ligaments and meniscus in a manner that is age and region dependent.
the distribution of biglycan, decorin, their mRNA, and collagen type I in the ligaments and meniscus of the rabbit knee changes with age, but not in the same way.
biglycan and, to a lesser extent, decorin are present in the matrix of all ligaments and meniscus, and their expression in the matrix is regulated by age and mechanical loading.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the distribution of biglycan is not uniform and it is not the same as decorin.
the small leucine rich proteoglycants are present in the extracellular matrix and that the expression of their mRNA’s is regulated by the cells in the matrix.
the small leucine rich proteoglycants are present at the time of birth, and that their expression is reduced in the ligaments and the menisci as they age.
